_note: The Hall is a Hall three days a week and a doss house the other four, which is a fact about Frostmere and not a joke about it. The child at the fire teaches the room's whole rule in three sentences and then says the important thing: that nobody would have told the player, and somebody should.

lines: Marked you back up. Both columns match and the book is straight.
Eira sent word that she is staying down a while. She always does, after one.
Down the stairs. Tell me when you go and tell me when you come back.
That is not a formality. Nobody has drowned under this house in two hundred years,
and every one of those years somebody sat at this desk writing names in a book.
Six in the morning, every cell, every day, whether or not it has changed.
The days it has not changed are the dangerous ones, because that is when you guess.
So I mark it anyway. Tick, tick, tick, cross, tick. My arm aches and the town drinks.
Pots on the ice: four. Four is a normal night. I have never been so glad of a number in my life.
Nineteen fires and not one hole stayed open. Four fires and all four of them do.
Do not ask me to explain it. I asked the Keeper and the Keeper said the same word I would have.
Pots on the ice: nineteen. We have never had more than eleven out at once.
Nineteen fires holding nineteen holes open, and the holes keep closing anyway,
and the ice round each one is getting worse and not better. Work that out for me.
You do not open a channel because you want a channel. You open it because of February.
In February this town takes its water out of holes in a floor. That is the whole reason.
Tick means you can. Cross means you cannot. No mark means there is nothing there.
I have known that since before I could read the words. Everybody here knows it.
You would not, though, would you. Nobody tells you. Somebody ought to tell you.
I am going home tomorrow. Our chimney is fine, our fuel is fine, and the house is going to be very quiet.
Sixteen bunks with somebody breathing in every one, for a fortnight. I am going to miss it and I know it.
I offered the Keeper money and was laughed at, so I have left it under a pot.
Our chimney is fine and our fuel is fine. I am here because the house is very quiet.
Sixteen bunks with somebody breathing in every one. It turns out that is the thing.
The Hall is a Hall three days a week and a doss house the other four.
Anywhere else in Caelora those would be two buildings. It has never occurred to us.
